cards.headline: Driver airlifted after single-car rollover on I-95 southbound near High Meadows in Palm City
cards.teaser: A driver was flown to the hospital by LifeStar with traumatic injuries Friday night after a single-car rollover crash on Interstate 95 southbound near the High Meadows exit in Palm
cards.body:
A driver was flown to the hospital by LifeStar with traumatic injuries Friday night after a single-car rollover crash on Interstate 95 southbound near the High Meadows exit in Palm City. Martin County Fire Rescue said the car crashed into a palm tree and rolled over onto its side. The crash occurred just after 6:15 p.m. near Mile Marker 102, near Florida's Turnpike.

 Martin County Fire Rescue's special operations team extricated the driver from the overturned vehicle. No other vehicles were involved in the collision. The Martin County Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol also responded to the scene.

 The nearest trauma center is HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce, which is 26 miles north. The closest Level 1 trauma center is St. Mary's Medical Center in West Palm Beach, about 38 miles south.

 All lanes of Interstate 95 southbound have been reopened. Martin County Fire Rescue posted on Facebook that C-Shift crews from Heavy Rescue 23, LifeStar, Alert 1, Rescue 211, Rescue 231, Engine 21, Engine 22, EMS 2, and Battalion 2 3 responded to the crash.

cards.headline: 17-year-old in custody after Indian River County shootout with 15-year-old, weapon recovered
cards.teaser: Deputies have taken a 17-year-old suspect into custody and recovered a short-barreled pistol following a shootout with a 15-year-old in a residential neighborhood. Video evidence confirms the two teens fired at each other in the middle of the street.
cards.body:
A 17-year-old suspect is in custody after a shootout with a 15-year-old in Indian River County, and deputies have recovered a short-barreled pistol believed to have been used in the incident. The 17-year-old was taken into custody Thursday morning following the Wednesday night shooting in the 1100 block of 12th Court Southwest. Kevin Jaworski with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office confirmed that investigators obtained video showing the two teenagers shooting at each other in the roadway.

 The shooting occurred at around 7:30 p.m. Wednesday after deputies responded to multiple 911 calls and found bullet casings at the scene. A nearby home and vehicle had been struck by gunfire. Julio Pitts, a resident in the area, said he was sitting in his living room when the shots rang out.

 Authorities believe the shootout stemmed from an ongoing feud between the two teens. Jaworski said the incident appears to be isolated and there is no threat to the community, but noted it was inherently dangerous because a car was hit, a house was hit, and anybody in those could have very well easily been hurt. The case remains under investigation.

hero.headline: Driver airlifted after single-car rollover on I-95 southbound near High Meadows in Palm City
hero.teaser: A driver was flown to the hospital by LifeStar with traumatic injuries Friday night after a single-car rollover crash on Interstate 95 southbound near the High Meadows exit in Palm
hero.body:
A driver was flown to the hospital by LifeStar with traumatic injuries Friday night after a single-car rollover crash on Interstate 95 southbound near the High Meadows exit in Palm City. Martin County Fire Rescue said the car crashed into a palm tree and rolled over onto its side. The crash occurred just after 6:15 p.m. near Mile Marker 102, near Florida's Turnpike.

 Martin County Fire Rescue's special operations team extricated the driver from the overturned vehicle. No other vehicles were involved in the collision. The Martin County Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol also responded to the scene.

 The nearest trauma center is HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce, which is 26 miles north. The closest Level 1 trauma center is St. Mary's Medical Center in West Palm Beach, about 38 miles south.

 All lanes of Interstate 95 southbound have been reopened. Martin County Fire Rescue posted on Facebook that C-Shift crews from Heavy Rescue 23, LifeStar, Alert 1, Rescue 211, Rescue 231, Engine 21, Engine 22, EMS 2, and Battalion 2 3 responded to the crash.

cards.headline: 17-year-old in custody after Indian River County shootout with 15-year-old, weapon recovered
cards.teaser: Deputies have taken a 17-year-old suspect into custody and recovered a short-barreled pistol following a shootout with a 15-year-old in a residential neighborhood. Video evidence confirms the two teens fired at each other in the middle of the street.
cards.body:
A 17-year-old suspect is in custody after a shootout with a 15-year-old in Indian River County, and deputies have recovered a short-barreled pistol believed to have been used in the incident. The 17-year-old was taken into custody Thursday morning following the Wednesday night shooting in the 1100 block of 12th Court Southwest. Kevin Jaworski with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office confirmed that investigators obtained video showing the two teenagers shooting at each other in the roadway.

 The shooting occurred at around 7:30 p.m. Wednesday after deputies responded to multiple 911 calls and found bullet casings at the scene. A nearby home and vehicle had been struck by gunfire. Julio Pitts, a resident in the area, said he was sitting in his living room when the shots rang out.

 Authorities believe the shootout stemmed from an ongoing feud between the two teens. Jaworski said the incident appears to be isolated and there is no threat to the community, but noted it was inherently dangerous because a car was hit, a house was hit, and anybody in those could have very well easily been hurt. The case remains under investigation.

cards.headline: Fellsmere woman, 75, wakes at 2:30 a.m. daily to feed stray cats, volunteers 60 hours a week at animal sanctuary
cards.teaser: Linn Stewart of Indian River County rises before dawn each morning to feed a colony of stray cats, then spends her days volunteering at For the Love of Paws in Fellsmere. The sanctuary provides free pet food to food banks, veterans, and seniors while caring for animals left behind by elderly owners.
cards.body:
Linn Stewart, a 75-year-old Indian River County resident, starts her day at 2:30 a.m. driving through the dark to feed her colony of stray cats. After the predawn feeding, Stewart volunteers 60 hours a week at For the Love of Paws in Fellsmere, a sanctuary for pets left behind by senior citizens who can no longer care for them.

 The sanctuary operates a pet food pantry that provides free pet food to food banks, veterans, and senior citizen organizations. Stewart and other volunteers cut open large bags and portion the food into four-pound bags. The sanctuary also provides medical care and flea medications when donations allow.

 Stewart, who lost both parents at age 30 and has little family nearby, said the work keeps her going. She has rescued animals all her life and now stops to help tortoises, turtles, and other wildlife she encounters. Stewart requires only four hours of sleep per night, a pattern she said began in childhood. Her dedication recently earned her recognition and a $525.25 award from Guardians.
